Mike Vermeulen

2026-05-25

Why this notebook exists

The HT1080 and A549 cell lines were each sequenced once, but the FASTQ files have been re-quantified through two different upstream pipelines at different points in the project. Per-cell-line analyses (2.1.1 A549, 2.2.1 HT1080) all use the NEW counts; older reports (in data/RNAseq/AUG_13_2025_LOY_A549_HT1080/) use the OLD counts. This notebook asks: how comparable are the two count tables, and would the biological conclusions change if we’d kept the OLD counts?

The “NEW” pipeline here is the current canonical one used by every downstream analysis (2.1.1 A549, 2.2.1 HT1080, 2.3.1 LNCaP): the PAR-aware STAR v2 realignment (STAR_v2_PARfix/). The interim non-PAR-aware STAR run (STAR_v1/) that briefly served as “NEW” between HISAT2 and the PAR-aware run is no longer in use; PAR1/PAR2 genes (SHOX, CSF2RA, SLC25A6, AKAP17A, …) were silently dropped at multi-mapper filtering in that interim run and are now recovered. Only HISAT2 (OLD) vs PAR-aware STAR (NEW) are compared here.

Pipeline difference summary

Field OLD pipeline NEW pipeline
Counts dir data/RNAseq/AUG_13_2025_LOY_A549_HT1080/counts/ projects/RNAseq/counts/STAR_v2_PARfix/AUG_2025_<cell>_LOY/
Aligner HISAT2 (default) STAR two-pass, PAR-Y-masked reference
chrY handling standard Y chromosome PAR regions hard-masked so chrX-PAR reads are no longer split between two equivalent positions
Reference annotation GENCODE v47 (chr_patch_hapl_scaff) GENCODE v49 (primary assembly)
featureCounts v2.0.1 v2.1.1
Sample composition identical (9 HT1080 + 11 A549) identical

Same biological samples; same FASTQs; different aligner + reference + quantifier + chrY handling. Differences between the two count tables are therefore technical — they tell us how much downstream interpretation is sensitive to the upstream pipeline choice, with particular emphasis on PAR1/PAR2 gene recovery (those genes are expected to drop to ~0 in the OLD pipeline and to be expressed at biologically plausible levels in the NEW one).

4. Gene-ID harmonization + filtering

The OLD pipeline annotated with GENCODE v47, NEW with v49. Both produce Ensembl IDs like ENSG00000123456.18 (with version suffix). The integer ENSG accession is stable across versions; the suffix changes when the gene’s annotation is updated. We harmonize by stripping the suffix and intersecting on the accession.

## --- HT1080 ----------------------------------------

##   NEW-unique ENSG: 24
##   Shared ENSG:     78875
## --- A549 ------------------------------------------

7. Sample correlation heatmap (concatenated OLD + NEW)

Concatenate OLD and NEW logCPM matrices for each cell line and cluster all samples together. Same biological sample under two pipelines should cluster together — and if pipeline effects dominate biology, we’d see OLD vs NEW samples cluster by pipeline instead.

## Saved: sample_cor_heatmap_A549.(png|pdf)

8. Differential expression on OLD vs NEW: do the conclusions change?

Three contrasts run on each pipeline’s counts:

  1. Paired LOY vs sgCTRL (~ 0 + treatment + passage) — canonical
  2. Unpaired LOY vs sgCTRL (~ 0 + treatment) — passage drift not modeled
  3. Pooled LOY vs (PARENTAL + sgCTRL) — combined Y+ baseline, n=6 vs n=3 (HT1080) or n=7 vs n=4 (A549)

Identical underlying biology under both pipelines → high logFC correlation and substantial DEG overlap regardless of which contrast we pick.

DE concordance: OLD vs NEW pipeline across three contrast types
cell contrast sig_OLD sig_NEW intersect jaccard lfc_r
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 621 578 551 0.8503 0.9850
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 65 66 61 0.8714 0.9856
HT1080 LOY vs pooled Y+ 92 91 83 0.8300 0.9885
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 11 9 9 0.8182 0.9753
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 9 8 8 0.8889 0.9804
A549 LOY vs pooled Y+ 10 7 7 0.7000 0.9889

9. GSEA — Hallmark NES concordance

If the upstream pipeline only shifts gene-level estimates within their noise envelope, the pathway-level NES should barely move. fgsea against the MSigDB Hallmark collection (50 sets) is run on a -sign(logFC) * -log10(P) rank for each of the 12 DE tables; OLD vs NEW NES are then scattered per contrast.

Hallmark NES concordance: OLD vs NEW pipeline (50 pathways)
cell contrast n_pathways sig_OLD sig_NEW intersect jaccard_sig nes_r sign_agree
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 50 19 19 19 1.000 0.973 0.96
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 50 12 9 9 0.750 0.918 0.92
HT1080 LOY vs pooled Y+ 50 16 15 15 0.938 0.925 0.92
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 50 13 12 12 0.923 0.977 0.98
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 50 11 16 11 0.688 0.948 0.94
A549 LOY vs pooled Y+ 50 23 26 23 0.885 0.985 0.98

10. TF regulons — CollecTRI activity concordance

Same idea, one layer up: feed the limma t-statistic (HGNC-keyed) for each of the 12 DE tables into decoupleR::run_ulm() against the CollecTRI regulon network. The result is a transcription-factor activity score per TF per contrast per pipeline; OLD vs NEW scores are scattered per contrast.

CollecTRI TF activity concordance: OLD vs NEW pipeline
cell contrast n_tfs sig_OLD sig_NEW intersect jaccard_sig score_r sign_agree
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 635 144 144 137 0.907 0.988 0.965
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 635 102 99 90 0.811 0.982 0.959
HT1080 LOY vs pooled Y+ 635 102 105 98 0.899 0.987 0.954
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 647 95 97 81 0.730 0.984 0.964
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 647 93 94 85 0.833 0.980 0.957
A549 LOY vs pooled Y+ 647 119 112 100 0.763 0.987 0.946
